sweep_method: No hard-block check fired, so there is no violation class to enumerate. Beyond the mechanical gates I swept four classes to closure rather than sampling: (1) all 39 migration names and all 40 SQL bodies compared base vs head by extraction, not by reading the diff; (2) all 63 RPC declarations and all 1701 non-comment proto lines compared; (3) all 17 workspace members classified publishable vs publish=false for lockstep; (4) all 11 removed-or-narrowed pub lines in crates/*/src enumerated from the diff and each individually resolved, with a tree-wide caller sweep for the one narrowing. One non-blocking class IS enumerated in the notes: four stale lease_now prose references.

tree-wide grep -rn 'lease_now\b' over all file types (excluding .git and target), plus base-vs-head provenance checks (git show db19a614:<file>, git blame, per-file diff filtering) on every hit, beyond the crates-only grep the brief specified; migration and proto invariants swept by full ordered-list and body comparison rather than spot checks

beyond the mechanical gates: full enumeration of the migration class (all 38 base vs 39 head names for rename/reorder, and every MIGRATION_* SQL constant body extracted and compared at both shas) and the full proto class (all 14 files, RPC declarations and non-comment lines); plus a tree-wide lease_now sweep over docs+crates+ci. No sweep was needed for the hard-block classes, which had zero violations.
